text:
Thomas Chabot has 12 points in 21 games, a pace above the middle of his talent range and well above the typical defenseman. Ottawa has carried play with him on the ice: 58% of the five-on-five expected goals, five points better than without him, a strong number for anyone logging 23:27 a night.

Some of the shine is luck. Ottawa has scored 5.9 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that tends to fade. His own scoring is light, two goals on 2.6 expected, with ten assists. What doesn't need luck is the defending: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him stopping 16% of the entries aimed at him, against 11% for a typical defenseman, and he has blocked 44 shots. Evolving-Hockey had him 29th among defensemen in wins above replacement last season. He has missed time this fall, and the headlines have tracked his returns closely. Our range projects 34 to 52 points.
